title: Raw fetch calls bypass the authenticated API client
reasoning: Several query functions construct raw fetch requests instead of using the shared api client used elsewhere in this group. The integration setup logs in and stores a token with the expectation that api.ts will apply it, and session integration also configures the axios api adapter, but raw fetch requests do not receive those auth headers, interceptors, adapter behavior, or any shared response handling. This can make authenticated query endpoints fail in real use even though adjacent mutations and session list calls succeed through api.
recommendation: Route these requests through the shared api client, or centralize an authenticated fetch helper that applies the same base URL, token, and error behavior as api.ts.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Unit tests mock global.fetch and assert only the URL, so they encode the unauthenticated request shape. The integration tests either skip without credentials or tolerate public endpoint behavior, and they do not assert that Authorization or shared api client behavior is used.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a unit test for fetchPart or fetchSessionParts that verifies the configured API client/auth path is used after a token is present, or mock the shared client and assert the request goes through it.
minimumFixScope: Update the raw fetch-based query functions that may require shared auth/config, starting with fetchPart and fetchSessionParts; consider applying the same pattern to explanation query reads for consistency.
